CVE-2026-104851.title: fsspec: Server-Side Template Injection in ReferenceFileSystem leads to Remote Code Execution
CVE-2026-104851.description: fsspec is a specification and Python implementation framework for filesystem interfaces. From 0.9.0 until 2026.6.0, fsspec.implementations.reference.ReferenceFileSystem evaluates fields from Kerchunk reference JSON documents through unrestricted jinja2.Template(...).render(...) calls in _process_references1._render_jinja, _process_templates, and _process_gen in fsspec/implementations/reference.py. A document supplied inline or fetched from an attacker-controlled URL can provide template expressions that execute Python code when the reference filesystem is opened, including through consumers such as xarray, before referenced data is read. The _process_gen path is reached whenever a document includes a gen array, while the other paths depend on template-related options and values. This issue is fixed in version 2026.6.0.

CVE-2026-119615.title: Reset Database <= 1.1.3 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Privilege Escalation to Missing Capability and Nonce Check in process_reset()
CVE-2026-119615.description: The Reset Database plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to privilege escalation in versions up to, and including, 1.1.3. This is due to the process_reset() function being registered on admin_init with no capability check, a computed-but-unused nonce, a gating condition that passes whenever no WordPress administrator literally named 'admin' exists (the default on modern installs), and an identity test that verifies the ATTACKER'S OWN password rather than an administrator's. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to drop every prefixed database table, re-run wp_install() with their own credentials — making the attacker the sole site administrator — authenticate as that administrator via wp_set_auth_cookie(), and delete the uploads directory.

CVE-2026-128127.title: AIOHTTP: Base64 multipart parts bypass client_max_size
CVE-2026-128127.description: AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, BodyPartReader.read_chunk() processing a multipart part with Content-Transfer-Encoding set to base64 keeps reading until the chunk length is a multiple of four without enforcing a byte limit. A short Content-Length or a long run of whitespace can cause one call to read the remaining body into memory before the size check or spin on the event loop. A remote attacker can send such a multipart request to a handler that reads multipart data and bypass client_max_size. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

CVE-2026-129502.title: @fastify/http-proxy vulnerable to Denial of Service via a URL fragment in a WebSocket upgrade
CVE-2026-129502.description: @fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.4.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, a WebSocket upgrade request whose path carries a URL fragment is matched by the router and answered with a successful upgrade before the upstream link is created. Building the upstream target then throws, the error is only logged, and the accepted client socket is left open with no error listener, so the next frame the client sends becomes an unhandled error and terminates the Node.js process. A request target that is not a valid URL reference reaching a parameterized prefix triggers the same path. A single unauthenticated upgrade request followed by one frame is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

CVE-2026-135107.title: Samba: smb2 pipe transceive allocates maxoutputresponse before the read
CVE-2026-135107.description: An **uncontrolled memory allocation** flaw has been found in the smbd_smb2_ioctl_pipe_write_done() function in source3/smbd/smb2_ioctl_named_pipe.c of the SMB2 named-pipe ioctl handling in the **Samba** package. The file server reserves memory for a named-pipe response using a size chosen by the client. It does not keep that size within the maximum the client and the server have already agreed. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can open a named pipe can request a very large response. The file server reserves that memory before it reads the pipe and holds it until the request ends. Repeating this on more connections can exhaust memory and keep the file service unavailable while those requests continue.

CVE-2026-71410.title: Use-After-Free in GNU Screen
CVE-2026-71410.description:
GNU Screen is vulnerable to a Use-After-Free in the utf8_handle_comb() function in encoding.c. Due to improper error handling during memory allocation failure, the global combchars pointer is freed but not reset to NULL. When a subsequent combining Unicode character arrives at the terminal, the function dereferences the freed pointer. An attacker who controls terminal content sent to the screen session, such as via a rogue SSH server or crafted escape sequences, can exploit this vulnerability to perform heap grooming and achieve arbitrary code execution.

This issue was fixed in version 5.0.2.

CVE-2026-99342.title: KVM: x86/xen: Enforce 4-byte alignment of vcpu_info registration
CVE-2026-99342.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86/xen: Enforce 4-byte alignment of vcpu_info registration

Xen's map_guest_area() enforces that vcpu_info is aligned to
sizeof(xen_ulong_t). KVM has no such check, allowing a guest to
register vcpu_info at an arbitrary byte alignment.

Enforce unconditional 4-byte alignment regardless of the current
shinfo mode. This is sufficient because subsequent commits ensure
that all locked atomic operations on vcpu_info fields use at most
32-bit accesses. Return -ENXIO on failure, matching Xen's
map_guest_area() behaviour for unaligned requests.

Originally observed in review of an unrelated patch:
https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260604193554.1BA311F00893@smtp.kernel.org/
